steps.name: Block in the blanket

lines.text: Let the windowsill, and the wall and the window frame dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Optional: lightly chalk its outline first, from the transfer outline in Before you start, measuring from the canvas edges with a ruler.
Inside the outlined area. Its bottom is about 1 in from the bottom edge, and its right side is at the right edge; it's about 15 in wide and 5 1/2 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the sleeping tabby cat, and the cat's shading and white patches will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the wooden windowsill and the frame's shadows, painted already: there, only soften this paint into their edge and leave them showing.
Paint: Golden yellow.
Brush: 1 inch flat.
Start with one simple shape (an oval, a circle, or a rectangle). Then add the rest in curved pieces on each side, like ( ), smaller toward the edges.
It should leave a shape made of distinct curved segments with small gaps or overlaps between them.

steps.meant: A flat golden-yellow blanket lies on the sill across the lower middle of the canvas, with no knit loops or shadows. The cat is not there yet.

steps.name: Tap in the dark knit loops

lines.text: Let the yellow knit blanket and the windowsill dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area. Its bottom is about 1 in from the bottom edge, and its right side is at the right edge; it's about 14 in wide and 5 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the sleeping tabby cat, and the cat's shading and white patches will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the yellow knit blanket, and the sill's shadow and sunlight, painted already: there, only soften this paint into their edge and leave them showing.
Paint: Dark ochre.
Brush: #8 round. Load: Creamy paint, a full load.
Touch down with the tip, press so the belly spreads, then pull and lift so the stroke ends on the tip.
It should leave a teardrop or comma shape, wide where you pressed and pointed where you lifted.
Watch out: A blob instead of a teardrop. Too much paint, or too slow a lift. Fix: use less paint and lift faster.

steps.meant: The golden blanket shows rows of dark ochre knit loops, densest under the roll and along the fold, with the gold showing between them. No light loops yet; no cat.

steps.name: Tap in the light knit loops

lines.text: Let the yellow knit blanket and the windowsill dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area. Its bottom is about 2 1/2 in from the bottom edge, and its left side is about 6 1/2 in from the left edge; it's under 1/4 in wide and under 1/4 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the sleeping tabby cat, and the cat's stripes and pink ears will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the yellow knit blanket, and the sill's shadow and sunlight, painted already: there, only soften this paint into their edge and leave them showing.
Paint: Pale yellow.
Brush: #6 round. Load: Creamy paint, a full load.
Touch down with the tip, press so the belly spreads, then pull and lift so the stroke ends on the tip.
It should leave a teardrop or comma shape, wide where you pressed and pointed where you lifted.
Leave what step 11 painted showing around these marks, as in the Result picture.
Watch out: A blob instead of a teardrop. Too much paint, or too slow a lift. Fix: use less paint and lift faster.
Step back, squint, or take a photo to see it whole, and compare the big shapes with the picture.

steps.meant: The blanket is finished: golden knit with dark ochre loops in its folds and pale yellow loops on the lit tops. The cat is not there yet; the blue wall shows where it will lie.
